title: International Organization, Regional Body, Grouping, Forum, Treaty — What's the Difference?
shortDescription: The classification exams actually test: organization vs grouping vs forum vs treaty vs specialized agency, before you meet a single acronym.
genZNote: Learn the categories first — otherwise G20 and WTO start feeling like the same kind of thing, and they're really not.

sections.heading: Why This Topic Comes First
sections.body: Competitive exams don't just ask 'what is the UN' — they ask questions that only make sense once you know WHAT KIND of body something is. Is BRICS an organization or a grouping? Is the Quad a treaty alliance? Is the Commonwealth the same category as the EU? Getting the category right is often the actual question, dressed up as a one-line MCQ.

sections.heading: The Core Categories
bullets: International (Intergovernmental) Organization — a permanent body created by a treaty between states, with its own charter, headquarters, staff, and legal personality. Example: the United Nations, WHO, WTO.

Specialized Agency — an independent international organization that has a formal working relationship with the UN through an agreement with ECOSOC, but is NOT part of the UN Secretariat and has its own membership and budget. Example: WHO, ILO, IMF, World Bank, UNESCO, ICAO.

UN Programme / Fund — created directly by a UN General Assembly resolution, reports to the GA/ECOSOC, and is funded mainly by voluntary contributions rather than a treaty of its own. Example: UNDP, UNICEF, UNEP, WFP, UNHCR.

Related Organization — works closely with the UN system but is fully autonomous and not a specialized agency. Example: IAEA (reports to the GA and Security Council under its own statute, not a specialized agency).

Regional Organization — membership is limited to states of a specific geographic region, and the mandate is usually broad (political, economic, security). Example: ASEAN, SAARC, African Union, European Union.

International Grouping / Forum — a loose, often informal coalition of countries that meets periodically to coordinate policy, usually WITHOUT a founding treaty, permanent headquarters, or full-time staff of its own. Example: G7, G20, BRICS, Quad.

Treaty / Convention / Agreement — a legally binding written agreement between states on a specific subject. It creates obligations but is not, by itself, an organization — though a treaty can ESTABLISH one (the UN Charter is a treaty that established the UN).
Alliance — a body focused specifically on collective defence/security commitments. Example: NATO is both a treaty (the North Atlantic Treaty, 1949) and the permanent organization it created.

sections.heading: Bodies Exams Love to Mislabel
bullets: G20 is a FORUM, not an organization — it has no charter, no permanent secretariat, and no standing headquarters; the host country rotates every year and runs it for that year only.
BRICS is a GROUPING — informal, no treaty, no headquarters, though it has since spun off a genuine institution: the New Development Bank (NDB), headquartered in Shanghai.

The Commonwealth is a voluntary ASSOCIATION of mostly-former British territories with a genuine Secretariat (in London) — closer to an organization than G20/BRICS are, but membership is symbolic/cultural rather than treaty-bound the way the EU is.
IAEA is NOT a UN specialized agency — it is a 'related organization' that reports directly to the UN General Assembly and Security Council under its own 1957 statute.
NATO is both a treaty (1949 North Atlantic Treaty) AND the permanent military-political organization that treaty created — it's correct to call it either, in context.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: An international organization has a treaty, charter, permanent headquarters and staff; a grouping/forum (like G20 or BRICS) has none of those and runs on rotating chairmanship and summits.
keyFacts: Specialized agencies (WHO, ILO, IMF, World Bank, UNESCO) are linked to the UN by agreement but are legally independent, with their own membership and budgets.
UN programmes/funds (UNDP, UNICEF, UNEP) are created by GA resolution and report to the GA/ECOSOC — they are not separate treaty organizations.
IAEA is a 'related organization', not a specialized agency.
G20 and BRICS are groupings with no charter and no permanent HQ; the NDB (BRICS-created) IS a real treaty-based institution.
commonConfusion: Don't call G20 or BRICS an 'organization' in an answer that's checking precise terminology — they are groupings/forums.
A treaty and the organization it creates are related but not identical — the North Atlantic Treaty (1949) created NATO; the treaty itself isn't 'NATO'.

highYieldFacts: Specialized agency = independent org with a UN linkage agreement; UN programme/fund = created directly by GA resolution.
G20 and BRICS have no charter and no permanent secretariat of their own — chairmanship rotates yearly.
IAEA reports to the UN GA and Security Council directly, as a 'related organization', not as a specialized agency.
commonTraps: Exams sometimes list G20 alongside 'organizations' like WTO/IMF in the same MCQ — the distractor usually tests whether you know G20 has no treaty basis.
Do not assume every UN-linked body is a 'specialized agency' — UNICEF, UNDP, UNEP are programmes/funds, not specialized agencies.
mustRemember: Treaty/charter + permanent HQ + staff = organization. No treaty, rotating chair, periodic summits only = grouping/forum.
The New Development Bank is the one genuine treaty-based institution to come out of the BRICS grouping.
possibleQuestions: Which of the following is NOT a UN specialized agency: WHO / UNICEF / ILO / UNESCO?
G20 is best classified as a(n): Specialized agency / Regional organization / International forum / Treaty organization?
